proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 p_E=\mathbb P_{z_0}(E),
 \qquad
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}].
\]
Membership in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), bounded wealth, and consistency imply \(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\) almost surely, so the displayed expectation is finite.  Since \(E\in\mathcal X\), the assumed equality \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\mathbf 1_E\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =b\mathbf 1_E
 \quad\mathbb P_{z_0}\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{1}
\]
The design-conditional-centering clause in \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} gives instead
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 =\mu_{si}
 \quad\mathbb P_{z_0}\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{2}
\]
Taking expectations in the shock representation yields
\[
 \mu_{si}=b\,\mathbb P_{z_0}(E)=bp_E.
\tag{3}
\]
Equations (1)--(3), followed by squaring and integration, imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[(b\mathbf 1_E-bp_E)^2]\\
 &=b^2\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[(\mathbf 1_E-p_E)^2]\\
 &=b^2p_E(1-p_E).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
Here the last equality uses \(\mathbf 1_E^2=\mathbf 1_E\).  Since \(b\ne0\), division by \(b^2\) in (4) gives \(p_E(1-p_E)=0\); because \(p_E\in[0,1]\), this is equivalent to \(p_E\in\{0,1\}\).

In the scalar kernel described in the statement,
\[
 \mathbb P_{z_0}(E)=\mathbb P_{z_0}(X_{11}\le q)=q\in(0,1).
\]
Taking \(b=b_*>0\) contradicts (4).  Hence that shocked kernel violates the centering clause and does not belong to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Event-date transport is not used.

Fix \(z_0\) and \(\mathbb P_{z_0}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), and put
\[
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}].
\]
Bounded wealth and consistency give \(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\) almost surely, so \(\mu_{si}\) is finite.  The design-conditional-centering clause of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid\mathcal X]=0.
\tag{1}
\]
For bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable \(W\), the pull-out and tower properties of conditional expectation yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W]
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}\!\left[
 W\,\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid\mathcal X)
 \right]\\
 &=0.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
This proves the asserted orthogonality.

Let \(E\in\mathcal X\) and set \(p_E=\mathbb P_{z_0}(E)\).  Taking \(W=\mathbf 1_E\) in (2) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf 1_E]=\mu_{si}p_E.
\tag{3}
\]
If \(p_E>0\), division by \(p_E\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E]=\mu_{si}.
\tag{4}
\]
Applying the same argument to \(E^c\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E^c]=\mu_{si}
\tag{5}
\]
when \(p_E<1\).  Equations (4)--(5) hold simultaneously for \(0<p_E<1\), and \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} gives the stated exclusion.  By \texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer}, every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) has a regular conditional kernel in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost every query.  Applying (1)--(5) to those kernels proves the panel-to-kernel transfer and makes no claim at a null-version query.

We now construct the two fixed-query kernels.  For arbitrary positive integers \(N,T,n_1\), take
\[
 S=1,
 \quad \pi_1=1,
 \quad H=0,
 \quad p=d=1,
 \quad z_0=\frac12,
 \quad \lambda=\kappa=1,
 \quad B=L=1,
 \quad \delta_0=\frac14,
\tag{6}
\]
and set \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), with any fixed \(\beta_0>0\) and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\).  These values satisfy all declared parameter ranges, and \(d=p(H+1)=1\).

On a product probability space let \((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T}\), \((\xi_j)_{j=1}^{N}\), and \((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1}\) be mutually independent, with
\[
 X_{1t}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(\xi_j=1)=\mathbb P(\xi_j=-1)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(\varepsilon_i=1)=\mathbb P(\varepsilon_i=-1)=\frac12.
\tag{7}
\]
Define
\[
 m_1(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Q_{1ti}=m_1(X_{1t})=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Z_j=\frac12+\xi_j.
\tag{8}
\]
For every event unit set \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\) and \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\).  Definition \texttt{def:buyhold-level} gives
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=\frac12.
\tag{9}
\]
Under \(\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\); under \(\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  In each case impose consistency by setting \(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1)\).  Then
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12
 \quad\text{under }\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)},
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12+\frac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad\text{under }\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}.
\tag{10}
\]
The smallest constructed return is \(-1/2>-1\), as required by the return support.

We verify membership in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(z_0)\).  Equations (8)--(10) imply
\[
 |Q_{1ti}|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(0)|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(1)|\le\frac34,
\tag{11}
\]
so bounded wealth holds.  The constant \(m_1\) has supremum norm \(1/2\), zero first derivative, and zero Holder seminorm; hence \(m_1\in\mathcal H_1(1,1)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac12,\partial[0,1]\right)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 f_{1t\mid z_0}(x)=1
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1].
\tag{12}
\]
Thus interior support and the query-conditional density bound hold.  The design dates are independent, so
\[
 \beta_1(k\mid z_0)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1.
\tag{13}
\]

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T})\).  Training outcomes are deterministic, and under the second kernel unit \(i\)'s event history depends only on \(\varepsilon_i\).  Independence in (7) therefore gives conditional independence of unit histories across \(i\), while
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{1ti}\mid\mathcal X]=\frac12=m_1(X_{1t}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =\mathbb E[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}].
\tag{14}
\]
Exact observation of each \(X_{1t}\) gives the center-only design property.  The donor sigma-field is generated by \((\xi_j)_j\), whereas the complete joint panel is generated by \((X_{1t})_t\) and, under the second kernel, \((\varepsilon_i)_i\).  Mutual independence in (7) therefore proves donor independence from the entire joint panel.

The donor conditions follow directly from (8):
\[
 \mathbb E Z_j=z_0=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j)=1,
 \qquad
 c_\Sigma I_1\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_1,
\tag{15}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4
 =\mathbb E|\xi_j|^4
 =1=B^4.
\tag{16}
\]
Finally, (9) and the definition of \(m_1\) give
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{1i}(0)]=\frac12=m_1(z_0),
\tag{17}
\]
so event-date transport holds.  Equations (8)--(17), together with imposed consistency, verify every clause of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}; hence
\[
 \mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)},\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}
 \in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(z_0).
\tag{18}
\]
If the query variable is taken to equal \(1/2\) almost surely and the conditional kernels are (18), the resulting laws \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\) satisfy every member property in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}; all query-conditional requirements are checked at their sole positive-probability query.  Thus \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\), without any appeal to a null conditional version.

The joint law of \(((X_{1t})_t,(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(Z_j)_j)\) is common to the two kernels by (7)--(8).  By \texttt{def:target}, (9)--(10), and \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tau_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)]=0,\\
 \tau_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)]
 =\frac14\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
Nevertheless, (10) and independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)
 =\frac1{16}\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i)
 =\frac1{16}.
\tag{20}
\]
Thus the fixed-query centered class permits different event-noise constants while holding the training experiment, donor experiment, and causal target fixed.  This proves the explicit certificate and the stated distinction between excluding the obsolete common-design shock and calculating a sharp minimax constant.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) and every regular conditional law \(P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\) of the complete causal-data array given the realized query, one has
\[
 P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)
\]
for \(P\)-almost every query value \(z_0\) under its marginal query law.  No membership assertion is made for a version of the conditional law at a query-null value.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) and a regular conditional law \(P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\).  We check the defining clauses of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}.  The consistency, boundedness, exact-design observation, Holder, and interior clauses hold under \(P\); disintegration therefore makes their conditional versions hold outside a marginally null set of query values.  The conditional-expectation equalities in \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} and \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} are equalities of versions and hence also hold outside marginally null sets.

Assumption \texttt{ass:design-density} explicitly supplies, for every \(s,t\), a conditional density satisfying
\[
 c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1]^d
\tag{1}
\]
for almost every query.  Assumption \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing} likewise supplies
\[
 \beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1,
\tag{2}
\]
for almost every query.  The conditional-independence assertions in \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}, \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, and \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} are precisely factorization assertions for these regular conditional laws.  Thus they hold for almost every query.  Finally, \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness}, \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, and \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} give, for almost every query,
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \quad
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid z_0)\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd},
 \quad
 \mathbb E\!\left[\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\mid z_0\right]\le B^4.
\tag{3}
\]

There are finitely many cohorts and dates and only countably many lags \(k\).  Intersecting the conull query sets just described therefore leaves a conull set.  At every query in this intersection, (1)--(3) and the remaining checked clauses are exactly the member properties of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Hence \(P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) there.  The argument deliberately says nothing about an arbitrarily selected conditional version on the complementary null set.
added_lemmas.justification: This lemma separates a fixed-query statistical experiment from the almost-everywhere disintegration that links it to a causal panel law.
added_lemmas.gap: It does not select or regularize conditional versions at query-null values.
added_lemmas.consumer: All fixed-query risk, coverage, and model-audit statements use this bridge when transferred back to the panel class.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix an admissible query \(z_0\).  Every kernel \(\mathbb P_{z_0}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}\!\left[
 \left\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\right\}W
 \right]=0
\]
for every cohort \(s\), unit \(i\), and bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable random variable \(W\).  Hence each \(E\in\mathcal X\) with \(0<\mathbb P_{z_0}(E)<1\) has the same treated mean on \(E\) and \(E^c\), and \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} excludes the former common-design-shock kernel. Nevertheless, there are admissible scalar fixed class parameters and, for every positive \(N,T,n_1\), two kernels \(\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)},\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(z_0)\), with corresponding degenerate-query laws \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\), having the same joint law of \((X_{1t},Q_{1ti},Z_j)\) and the same target \(\tau(z_0)=0\), while
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=\frac1{16}.
\]
Thus removal of the invalid witness is a necessary model repair, not a determination of the sharp constants for the remaining centered fixed-query product experiment.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The previous theorem did not distinguish a fixed-query kernel from a panel regular conditional law and therefore appeared to assert results at arbitrary null-version queries. proposed.name: \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\)
proposed.construction:
Fix a deterministic query \(z_0=(z_{01}^{\top},\ldots,z_{0S}^{\top})^{\top}\in([0,1]^d)^S\).  Define \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) to be the class of probability laws \(\mathbb P_{z_0}\) for the complete causal-data array at this fixed query for which the following pointwise conditions hold.  First, for every \(s,i\),
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\ \text{almost surely},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}),
\]
\(|Q_{sti}|\vee|B_{si}(0)|\vee|B_{si}(1)|\le B\) almost surely, \(m_s\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and every \(X_{st}\) is observed exactly.  Second, for every \(s,t\), \(X_{st}\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_{st\mid z_0}\) satisfying
\[
 c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1]^d,
\]
and, for every \(s\), the sequence \((X_{st})_{t=1}^{T}\) has beta-mixing coefficients \(\beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\) for all \(k\ge1\).  Third, with \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{u,v})\), unit histories are conditionally independent across \((s,i)\) given \(\mathcal X\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}].
\]
Fourth, the donors are independent and identically distributed, are independent of the entire joint panel \(((X_{st})_{s,t},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i})\), and satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}Z_j=z_0,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}(Z_j),
 \qquad
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\le B^4.
\]
This is a class of fixed-query kernels, not a choice of a regular conditional version at a query-null value.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Fixed-query minimax suprema and expected-length statements need a version-invariant pointwise parameter space.

proposed.name: Fixed-query independent-calendar subclass
proposed.construction:
For each fixed admissible query \(z_0\), define
\[
 \mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)
 =\left\{\mathbb P_{z_0}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0):
 (X_{s1},\ldots,X_{sT})\text{ are independent under }\mathbb P_{z_0}
 \text{ for every }s\right\}.
\]
Only the design dates are required to be independent.  Responses may remain arbitrarily dependent across dates within a unit history.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The no-log subclass must be stated at the same fixed-query kernel level as the random-design frontier.

proposed.name: Fixed-query geometric-mixing marginal squared-risk scale
proposed.construction:
At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), define
\[
 R_{\mathrm{or}}
 =\left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}
 \vee
 \left[\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right]^2
 \vee
 \left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{2\lambda/d},
 \qquad
 R_\star=R_{\mathrm{or}}\vee N^{-\kappa}.
\]
The quantity \(R_\star\) is the marginal oracle-plus-donor squared-risk scale over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Its final component is the full-covariance generated-query contribution, while the last component of \(R_{\mathrm{or}}\) is the worst-case pointwise spacing scale under geometric design beta mixing.  Over \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), replace that spacing component by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The rate definition must identify its fixed-query uniformity domain and its oracle-plus-donor interpretation.

proposed.name: Fixed-query product-experiment ordered-modulus handle
proposed.construction: At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), solve the ordered-modulus problem for the product of the treated-mean, bounded replicated-regression, realized-design, and full-covariance donor-location experiments induced by \(\mathbb P_{z_0}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Invert the resulting least-favorable tests using either the whole unit history as the stochastic coordinate or a valid deterministic product-experiment test.  No calendar-block score, response-block independence, or conditioning on a query-null version is part of this handle.

 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=\frac1{16}.
\]
Thus removal of the invalid witness is a necessary model repair, not a determination of the sharp constants for the remaining centered fixed-query product experiment.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper delivers a fixed-query minimax and honest-length frontier for the rough Holder regime \(0<\lambda\le1\), where \(\kappa=\lambda\). At each admissible query \(z_0\), all uniform random-design statements are over the named conditional-kernel class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\); a separate bridge transfers them to each causal panel law only for almost every realized query. Consistency and the explicitly untestable event-date transport equality identify the cohort-weighted buy-and-hold contrast. The nonredundant rate channels are treated replication, query-conditional calendar spacing, and full-covariance donor location. The feasible interval concentrates independent whole-unit histories and has no calendar-score branch. Conditional design independence removes the geometric-mixing logarithm. Higher-order signed-weight stability for \(\lambda>1\), uniform-in-query claims, and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical fixed-point regression does not combine replicated sites with an external full-covariance generated query, and a panel-law regular conditional distribution is not defined pointwise at query-null values. Existing ordinary-regression and synthetic-control intervals also do not justify globally design-selected calendar scores as independent blocks.
project_justification.niche: Historical paths can be recorded exactly while only the event-date counterfactual path is synthesized from donors. A named fixed-query kernel class makes the statistical frontier version invariant, while an almost-everywhere bridge keeps the causal panel interpretation honest. In the rough Holder regime this separates exact-design recovery, query-conditional spacing, donor-location uncertainty, and the untestable causal transport equality.
project_justification.fill: The note defines \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) using pointwise conditional density, design-mixing, centering, donor-factorization, ellipticity, support, and causal restrictions at an admissible query. It proves conditional, marginal, and honest-length rate frontiers for \(0<\lambda\le1\) over that class and transfers them to every panel law for almost every query. A nearest-site rule and an anchor/extrapolation rule attain the risk rates. The honest interval uses whole-unit bounded-range concentration, generated-center bias calibration, and total fallbacks; matching lower bounds use explicit treated, spacing, and overlapping full-covariance donor pairs.

sampling_model.design: The pointwise statistical model is the kernel class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) at a fixed admissible query. For each cohort and date, the exact pre-event path has a density between \(c_X\) and \(C_X\) for Lebesgue-almost every design point, uniformly over these kernels, and each cohort's design sequence is geometrically beta mixing. The independent-calendar subclass imposes independence only on design dates under the fixed-query kernel. For a joint panel law, these conditions and all conclusions are asserted only at almost every query supplied by its regular conditional law.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks per date and \(n_s\) treated event outcomes. Under a fixed-query kernel and conditional on the exact design, unit histories are independent across units and have the stated conditional means. Dependence across all training dates and the event outcome within one unit history remains unrestricted; inference treats that whole history as one bounded observation.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth. Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path. Neither fixed-query design regularity nor design-conditional centering establishes this causal equality, and the panel-law interpretation is only query-almost-everywhere.
sampling_model.overlap: Every fixed query admitted to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary. Exact fixed-design recovery can be easier than an anchor bandwidth suggests when a site equals the query. The regular donor-location converse requires \(\delta_0<1/2\), because otherwise the admissible displacement can collapse.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event query is generated: deterministic donor folds produce projected means, and the full stacked covariance retains cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort dependence. At a fixed query, donors are independent of the entire joint design-response-event panel, so further design conditioning preserves donor independence from unit histories. For \(0<\lambda\le1\), local-constant weights are nonnegative with unit absolute mass; whole-unit concentration is therefore sufficient and avoids deconvolution, calendar-score studentization, and response-mixing assumptions.

prose_updates.related_work: Donoho (1994) relates a linear-functional modulus to minimax recovery in a known Gaussian convex experiment; the conditional theorem instead constructs a bounded replicated-response product experiment with an external full-covariance query, nearest-site geometry, and a separate almost-everywhere causal bridge. Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study independently estimated minimizers under strong convexity, making center error second order rather than a rough-Holder donor modulus. Stone (1982), Fan (1993), Fan et al. (1997), and Gaiffas (2007) provide ordinary Holder, pointwise local-polynomial, kernel-efficiency, and random-design sup-norm benchmarks; none supplies a fixed-query replicated-panel frontier with generated location. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012), Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008), and Fan and Truong (1993) perturb every training coordinate, unlike the exact historical design here; Hahn and Ridder (2013) gives smooth generated-regressor expansions rather than this nonsmooth modulus. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) provide ordered-modulus and bias-aware ordinary-regression interval benchmarks, while Low (1997) motivates fixing the smoothness class rather than claiming adaptation. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021), Kunsch (1989), and Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu (2021) concern dependent prediction, resampling, or conformal architectures; none is used for calendar calibration here, because the repaired interval concentrates independent whole-unit histories. Ferman (2021) motivates many-control replication. Abadie (2021) and Arkhangelsky and Imbens (2024) frame panel causal assumptions but neither validates event-date transport nor supplies the fixed-query statistical frontier.
prose_updates.interpretation: The fixed-query class separates exact-site geometry from uncertainty in a generated donor query without selecting arbitrary null versions of a panel regular conditional law. Query-conditional density and design mixing ensure that an admissible query cannot systematically select an unregulated design hole. Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and spacing. For any causal panel law, this interpretation transfers only at almost every realized query. Inference needs no calendar response mixing: after fixing the admissible query, selected design, and donors, it concentrates across independent unit histories while allowing arbitrary temporal response dependence within a unit.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Every constructive headline is restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\) and to fixed admissible queries in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\); panel-law statements hold only almost everywhere in the query and are not uniform-in-query bands. For \(\lambda>1\), higher-order fixed-design recovery uses signed weights whose conditional stochastic norm is not controlled by the present assumptions. Geometric conditional design mixing retains the logarithmic spacing penalty; only conditional design independence yields the no-log term. The donor converse requires \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\). The unit-history interval is rate-optimal but conservative, and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Event-date transport is an untestable causal restriction. Query-conditional density and design mixing are observed-law restrictions encoded pointwise in the fixed-query kernel class, while design-conditional centering is a separate response condition. Donor-panel separation factors donors from the complete joint panel and leaves dependence within each unit's training-event history unrestricted. Risk, coverage, and expected-length statements are uniform over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) at each admissible fixed query; for a joint panel law they transfer only for almost every query, with no claim at a null conditional version. The interval uses no calendar-score branch or estimated-variance division. Higher smoothness, growing dimension, adaptation, uniform-in-query bands, and exact constants are outside scope.

Put \(q=Sd\) and \(\Delta_B=B^4-q^2>0\).  Choose \(a_D>1\) so that
\[
 1<a_D^2<1+\Delta_B/2.                                            \tag{1}
\]
For \(|u|\) in a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of zero, define
\(V_u\in\{-a_D,0,a_D\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}+\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}-\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a_D^2}.                                   \tag{2}
\]
The probabilities are positive after shrinking the neighborhood, and direct
summation gives
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=u,\qquad\operatorname{Var}(V_u)=1.                  \tag{3}
\]
Let the other \(q-1\) coordinates be independent Rademacher variables.  At
\(u=0\),
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_0^{(q)}\|_2^4
 =a_D^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2-1+a_D^2<B^4.                           \tag{4}
\]
The centered fourth moment is continuous in \(u\), so the strict bound
persists on a smaller fixed neighborhood.

Put \(z^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_q\) and
\(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\delta_Ne_1\), where
\(\delta_N=c_*N^{-1/2}\).  Since \(\delta_0<1/2\), both paths are
interior for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Under alternative
\(v\in\{0,1\}\), take i.i.d. donors whose first coordinate is
\(1/2+V_{v\delta_N}\) and whose remaining coordinates are \(1/2\) plus the
common Rademacher coordinates.  Then
\[
 \mathbb E_vZ_j=z^{(v)},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_v(Z_j)=I_q,\qquad
 \mathbb E_v\|Z_j-z^{(v)}\|_2^4\le B^4.                           \tag{5}
\]
Because \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), the full covariance is uniformly
elliptic.

The square roots of the three probabilities in (2) have bounded second
derivatives near zero, their affinity equals one at zero, and its first
derivative is zero.  Thus the one-donor Hellinger affinity is at least
\(1-C_0\delta_N^2\).  Product factorization and the Cauchy--Schwarz
total-variation inequality give
\[
 \|P_1^{Z,N}-P_0^{Z,N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\{1-(1-C_0\delta_N^2)^{2N}\}^{1/2}.                           \tag{6}
\]
Choosing fixed \(c_*>0\) sufficiently small makes (6) at most
\(1-\eta_0\) for some fixed \(\eta_0>0\).

Use a common i.i.d. uniform exact training design.  If
\(0<\kappa<1\), set
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)_+^\kappa;
\]
if \(\kappa=1\), use the affine function
\(m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)\).  Set all other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).
For \(\lambda<1\), \(\kappa=\lambda\) and the positive-part power is
\(\lambda\)-Holder.  For \(\lambda\ge1\), the affine surface belongs to
every stated Holder class.  Sufficiently small positive \(b_0,b_1\), chosen
in terms of \(B,L\), enforce the Holder radius and boundedness, and
\[
 |m_1(z^{(1)}_1)-m_1(z^{(0)}_1)|=b_1\delta_N^\kappa.               \tag{7}
\]
Use identical bounded centered training noise, the same training design,
and identical positive constant treated observations under both laws.  Set
\(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and the unobserved untreated event wealth
to \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\).  Taking \(W_{si,-1}=1\),
\(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\) realizes
these wealth levels under \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.

We verify membership.  The uniform design has conditional density one
Lebesgue-almost everywhere, uniformly over dates and cohorts, and its
conditional beta-mixing coefficients are zero.  Thus the corrected
\texttt{ass:design-density} and \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing} hold at the
constant query under each law.  The constructions above verify boundedness,
Holder smoothness, consistency, event-date transport, and conditional
centering.  Unit histories are independent across \((s,i)\), while arbitrary
dependence inside each chosen history is allowed.  The donor primitive is
independent of the design, all training responses, and all treated outcomes,
so \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} holds for the complete joint
panel.  Donor independence, unbiasedness, ellipticity, and the fourth-moment
bound follow from (5).  Hence both laws are in
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).

The observed panel factors are identical and (6) controls the only differing
observed factor.  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (7) give
\[
 |\tau_1(z^{(1)})-\tau_0(z^{(0)})|
 =\pi_1b_1c_*^\kappa N^{-\kappa/2}.                               \tag{8}
\]
This proves the two-law certificate without a class-wide lower local
modulus.

Put \(q=Sd\).  Since \(B^4\ge q^2\), the common donor law
\(Z_j=z_0+U_j\), with independent Rademacher coordinates in \(U_j\), has
mean \(z_0\), covariance \(I_q\), and
\(\mathbb E\|U_j\|_2^4=q^2\).  Take it independent of the entire joint
panel.

Choose \(\gamma>0\) so small that \(e^{-\gamma}>2\alpha\), and define
\[
 L_T=\left\lfloor
 \frac{\log T-2\log\log(T\vee3)}{|\log\rho_0|}
 \right\rfloor\vee1,
 \qquad p_T=\frac{\gamma L_T}{T}.                                \tag{1}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), the definition of \(L_T\) implies
\[
 2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}.                                   \tag{2}
\]
Partition the first cohort's calendar into complete consecutive blocks of
length \(L_T\).  Independently label each complete block by
\(C_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Let \(A_T\) be the cube centered
at \(z_{01}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_d\) having volume \(p_T\).  Conditional on
\(C_b=1\), draw every design point in that block independently uniformly on
\(A_T\); conditional on \(C_b=0\), draw them independently uniformly on
\(A_T^c\).  Every complete-block marginal density equals
\[
 p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
 +(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1                      \tag{3}
\]
Lebesgue-almost everywhere.  Draw the incomplete block and all other cohorts
independently and uniformly.  Thus the conditional density bounds hold
uniformly.

If \(k<L_T\), past and future sigma-fields separated by \(k\) dates share
at most one Bernoulli block label.  Replacing that label by an independent
copy changes the joint law in total variation by at most \(2p_T\); this
follows directly by conditioning on the two values of the label.  If
\(k\ge L_T\), the sigma-fields use disjoint labels and are independent.
Because \(\rho_0^k\ge\rho_0^{L_T-1}\) for \(k<L_T\), (2) yields
\[
 \beta(k)\le2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}
 \le\beta_0\rho_0^k,\qquad k<L_T,                                \tag{4}
\]
and the desired inequality is trivial for \(k\ge L_T\).

Let \(E_T\) be the event that every complete-block label is zero and that no
point in the incomplete block lies in a fixed smaller concentric cube.  The
incomplete-block failure probability is at most \(L_Tp_T=o(1)\), while
\[
 \Pr(E_T)=(1-p_T)^{\lfloor T/L_T\rfloor}-o(1)
 \longrightarrow e^{-\gamma}>
 \eta_\alpha:=\frac{e^{-\gamma}+2\alpha}{2}>2\alpha.              \tag{5}
\]
Let \(h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\) be the side scale of the smaller cube.  Choose
a fixed smooth bump \(\phi\), supported inside the unit rescaling of this
cube, with \(\phi(0)=1\).  For sufficiently small fixed \(a,b_0>0\), put
\[
 m_{10}(x)=b_0,\qquad
 m_{11}(x)=b_0+ah_T^\lambda\phi((x-z_{01})/h_T),                   \tag{6}
\]
and keep all other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).  A derivative of order \(j\)
of the perturbation is of order \(h_T^{\lambda-j}\), and its highest-order
Holder seminorm is bounded independently of \(T\).  Thus a fixed small
\(a\) puts both surfaces in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\); small
\(a,b_0\) also enforce bounded wealth.

Under alternative \(v\), set \(Q_{1ti}=m_{1v}(X_{1t})\), use the common
constant surfaces elsewhere, keep positive treated observations identical,
impose consistency, and set untreated event wealth equal to
\(m_{sv}(z_{0s})\).  Baseline wealth one, horizon-zero return equal to wealth
minus one, and later returns zero give the required buy-and-hold levels.  The
conditional centering equalities hold by construction, and conditional on
the design the unit histories are degenerate and therefore mutually
independent.  Equations (3)--(4) prove the corrected conditional design
conditions.  The donors factor from the complete joint panel and satisfy all
donor bounds.  Hence both laws belong to the frozen panel class.

On \(E_T\), no response is evaluated in the bump support.  The restrictions
of the two observed laws to \(E_T\) coincide, giving a common subprobability
measure of mass at least \(\eta_\alpha\) for all sufficiently large \(T\).
Finally, \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (6) yield
\[
 |\tau_1(z_0)-\tau_0(z_0)|
 =\pi_1ah_T^\lambda
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.        \tag{7}
\]
This is the required common-submeasure certificate.

By \texttt{def:target},
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \left\{\mathbb E[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]
             -\mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\right\}.                 \tag{1}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} gives
\(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) almost surely, hence equality of the
corresponding conditional expectations at every query value where the
chosen regular conditional expectations are defined:
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]
 =\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].                          \tag{2}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} separately gives
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]=m_s(z_{0s}).                           \tag{3}
\]
Substituting (2)--(3) into the finite sum (1) proves
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \left\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\right\}.
\]
Thus the observed-law functional is derived from the causal contrast and is
not its definition.  No design-density, mixing, donor, rank, or inversion
condition is used.

Put \(q=Sd\) and
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda.          \tag{1}
\]
We first work in the deterministic experiment
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  Fix
\(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\).  Conditional on the donor sample, define
\[
 U_{si}=E_{si}-\mu_s-K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.                       \tag{2}
\]
The donor sample is independent of all unit histories, and the histories are
independent across \((s,i)\).  Thus (2) is conditionally centered and
independent across \((s,i)\).  Boundedness gives \(|U_{si}|\le4B\), whence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\!\left(
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(Z_j)_j\right)\le16B^2A.                            \tag{3}
\]

Let \(t_s^0\) be the smallest nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  By the
definition of \(t_{s\ell}\),
\[
 \|X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_s\|_2
 \le\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2
      +2\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2.                           \tag{4}
\]
Since \(0<\lambda\le1\), powers of order \(\lambda\) are subadditive.
Holder continuity and (4) yield
\[
 |f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-f_s(z_s)|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda+
 \|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda+
 \|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2^\lambda\}.                      \tag{5}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive, each balanced fold has size at
least \(N/3\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)\le qC_\Sigma\), so
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z\|_2^2
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{|I_\ell|}
 \le\frac{3qC_\Sigma}{N}.                                        \tag{6}
\]
The experiment also imposes \(\|z-z_0\|_2^2\le C_\Sigma/N\).
Expanding \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\)
into the centered sum (3) and the approximation terms (5), then using Jensen
in (6), proves
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}
 .                                                                \tag{7}
\]
Measurability of the nearest-design rule proves the first minimax inequality.
When \(\delta_0<1/2\),
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} makes the right side of
(7) at most \(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).

For the lower bound, first note the following elementary consequence of
total variation.  If \(P_0,P_1\) have targets separated by \(\Delta\) and
\(\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1-\eta\), then, for
\(A_0=\{|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\),
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\theta-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\}
 \ge\frac{\eta\Delta^2}{8}.                                     \tag{8}
\]
The first inequality follows because on \(A_0\) the error under law one is
at least \(\Delta/2\), and on its complement the error under law zero is at
least \(\Delta/2\); the second is the variational definition of total
variation.

For the treated-mean channel, keep responses and donors fixed and, under
\(v\in\{-1,1\}\), take independent \(E_{si}\in\{-b,b\}\), where
\(0<b<B\), with
\[
 \Pr_v(E_{si}=b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.             \tag{9}
\]
Since \(A\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma\) makes all
probabilities lie in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The target separation is
\(4\gamma\sqrt A\).  Their Hellinger affinity is
\[
 \prod_{s=1}^{S}(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge\exp(-C\gamma^2/b^2)>0,                                      \tag{10}
\]
because \(\sum_sn_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  The
Cauchy--Schwarz bound (7) in the proof of
\texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} makes total variation uniformly
smaller than one.  Equation (8) gives risk at least \(cA\).

For the fixed-design channel set
\[
 q_s(x)=a_0\min_{1\le t\le T}\|x-X_{st}\|_2^\lambda,
\]
with \(a_0>0\) small in terms of \(B,L,d\), and take
\(f_s=q_s/2\), \(g_s=-q_s/2\).  The argument (6)--(8) of
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} shows that these
surfaces lie in the class and agree at every design site.  Deterministic zero
responses, identical event laws, and identical donors therefore give
identical observations while the targets differ by \(a_0D_X\).  Equation
(8) yields risk at least \(cD_X^2\).

For the donor channel apply \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} under
the strict interior and moment slack, with any fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\).  Its
one-coordinate displacement lies in a cohort \(s_0\), say in coordinate
\(k\).  Under both laws use
\[
 f_{s_0}(x)=a_1|x_k-z_{0,s_0k}|^\lambda,
 \qquad f_s(x)=0\quad(s\ne s_0),                                  \tag{11}
\]
with \(a_1\) small enough for the Holder and boundedness restrictions.  Keep
the response and event laws identical.  The product total variation is at
most \(1-\eta\), whereas the target separation is at least
\(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Equation (8) yields risk at least
\(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Maximizing the three lower bounds and invoking (11) of
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} proves the deterministic
lower bound.

We next establish the fixed-query-kernel bridge.  Fix admissible \(z_0\) and
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Let \(\mathcal X\) denote the
exact-design sigma-field, \(\mathcal H\) all unit histories, and
\(\mathcal Z\) the donor sigma-field.  By the definition of the fixed-query
class, \(\mathcal Z\) is independent of \(\mathcal X\vee\mathcal H\), and
the unit histories are conditionally independent across \((s,i)\) given
\(\mathcal X\).  The two centering equalities, boundedness, and the donor
moment and covariance restrictions therefore show that, for
\(\mathbb K_\xi\)-almost every \(X\), the conditional observed law with its
labels is in \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\), at its central point
\(z=z_0\).  Its statistical target is
\[
 \theta_{\mathfrak E}
 =\sum_s\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0).                                 \tag{12}
\]
Applying (7) conditionally proves the fixed-query nearest-design bound; under
\(\delta_0<1/2\), the geometry lemma converts it to the
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\) bound.

If each design contains \(z_{0s}\), then \(D_X=0\), and the exact-site
claim follows from the geometry lemma.  Suppose instead
\(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Then
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is feasible in every foldwise anchor search, so
certificate optimality gives
\[
\begin{split}
 &C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V\{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}.
\end{split}                                                         \tag{13}
\]
The floor makes the last term no larger than \((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).
Since \(r=0\), the fit weights are nonnegative and sum to one.  Holder
continuity bounds approximation bias by the first two terms on the left of
(13); whole-history conditional independence bounds variance by \(CA\).
Donor unbiasedness, (6) at \(z=z_0\), Jensen's inequality, and (13) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2\mid\mathcal X]
 \le CR_D.                                                        \tag{14}
\]
The final assertion of the geometry lemma gives
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).

Finally fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  By the two corrected
query-conditional assumptions and the remaining conditional member
properties, there is a common full-marginal-measure set of admissible query
values on which its labelled regular conditional kernel satisfies every
condition in \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}; hence it belongs to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Assumption
\texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} is crucial here: it factors donors
from the entire joint panel, so the factorization remains valid after
conditioning on \(\mathcal X\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification}
gives \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) on the same set.  Equations
(12)--(14) therefore transfer to the causal conditional kernel for almost
every query and almost every exact design.  This argument never chooses a
regular conditional version on a query-null set.

Write
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_T=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}.      \tag{1}
\]
Fix \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\) and
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  On the event that every
reference anchor \((z_{0s},1)\) is coercive, the set defining
\(g_{sT}(z_0)\) is nonempty, its minimizing pair
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is feasible in every foldwise anchor search, and
certificate optimality gives (13) in
\texttt{thm:conditional-frontier}.  The same Holder-bias and whole-history
variance calculation as in (14) then gives conditional squared risk at most
\(CR_D\).  On the complement,
clipping and boundedness put both the estimator and target in \([-2B,2B]\),
so squared error is at most \(16B^2\).  The uniform fallback and moment
bounds in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment}, the bandwidth-floor
inequality, and Minkowski's inequality therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \le C\bigg[&A+
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2\\
 &+D_T+N^{-\lambda}\bigg]
 \le CR_\star.
\end{aligned}                                                       \tag{2}
\]
Here \(T^{-2}\le CD_T\).  Uniformity in the anchor lemma makes (2) uniform
over \(z_0\) and \(\xi\).

The smoothing display is redundant.  With \(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and
\(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\),
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.                                                    \tag{3}
\]
Since \(S\) is fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2
 \le2S\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}+2T^{-2\lambda/d}
 \le C(A+D_T).                                                     \tag{4}
\]

For completeness, if two laws have targets separated by \(\Delta\) and
total variation at most \(1-\eta\), the event that an estimator lies within
\(\Delta/2\) of the first target and the variational definition of total
variation give
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\tau-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\eta\Delta^2/8.                                               \tag{5}
\]
Assume now \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\).  For the treated channel,
fix \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf1\), take conditionally independent uniform
designs, a common admissible donor law, constant untreated surfaces, and the
two bounded event laws (9)--(10) from the proof of
\texttt{thm:conditional-frontier}.  Translate their support into a positive
subinterval of \((-B,B)\), set treated potential wealth equal to observed
wealth, and set untreated event wealth equal to the constant surface.
Baseline wealth one, the horizon-zero return equal to wealth minus one, and
later returns zero verify \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.  Thus both labelled
kernels lie in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), their separation is
\(cA^{1/2}\), and (5) yields risk at least \(cA\).

The construction proved in \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family}
has constant query values \(z^{(0)}\) and \(z^{(1)}\), and its proof verifies
the corrected pointwise conditional conditions at each.  Hence its two
labelled regular conditional kernels lie respectively in
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z^{(0)})\) and
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z^{(1)})\).  Because the decision rule is
chosen before the supremum over query values, (5) and that lemma give the
lower term \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Likewise,
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} has one fixed query,
and its two kernels are in the same fixed-query class; its common
subprobability measure and target separation give the lower term \(cD_T\).
Together with the treated channel and (4),
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{z_0}\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \asymp A\vee D_T\vee N^{-\lambda}\asymp R_\star.                \tag{6}
\]

On the independent-calendar subclass, the last part of the anchor lemma
replaces \(D_T\) in (2) by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  For the converse, use an
i.i.d. uniform design and a cube of radius \(r_T=cT^{-1/d}\) around
\(z_{01}\).  Two bounded Holder surfaces can agree outside this cube and
differ at its center by \(c_1r_T^\lambda\).  At each date the hit probability
is at most \(v_dr_T^d\); hence, for sufficiently small fixed \(c\),
\[
 \Pr\{X_{1t}\text{ misses the cube for every }t\}
 =(1-p_T)^T\ge c_2>0.                                             \tag{7}
\]
On this event the two observed laws coincide, while their targets differ by
\(c_1T^{-\lambda/d}\).  Equation (5) yields the lower squared-risk term
\(cT^{-2\lambda/d}\).

In the scalar specialization, (2) before the reduction is
\[
 n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}
 \vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
Equation (4) shows that its smoothing term is dominated by the maximum of
the first and third terms.  Finally, for each panel law, the almost-everywhere
kernel membership and equality
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau\) were proved in
\texttt{thm:conditional-frontier}; applying (2) to that kernel proves the
causal transfer without evaluating a null conditional version.

Fix \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\) and
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Write
\(\mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Boundedness
implies \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\in[-2B,2B]\).  On the regular
branch, \(r=0\).  Conditional on the exact design and donor sample, the
selected weights are response-independent, nonnegative, and obey
\(\sum_tw_{st}=1\).  Define one variable per complete unit history by
\[
 \zeta_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\left[
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_s
 -\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}\right].              \tag{1}
\]
Donor--panel independence means that conditioning further on donors does not
change the conditional unit-history law given the design.  The two centering
equalities in the fixed-query class center (1), and its cross-unit condition
makes the variables independent across \((s,i)\).  Their range lengths are
at most
\[
 d_{si}=\frac{2B\pi_s}{n_s}
 \left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right).                            \tag{2}
\]
For \(V\in[a,b]\), convexity of the exponential gives
\(\mathbb E\exp\{u(V-\mathbb EV)\}\le
\exp\{u^2(b-a)^2/8\}\).  Exponential Markov optimization,
independence, (2), and the definition of \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) imply
\[
 \Pr\left\{\left|\sum_{s,i}\zeta_{si}\right|>r_{\mathrm{unit}}
 \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal X,(Z_j)_j\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}.                                        \tag{3}
\]
The positive linear term in \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) only enlarges the
Hoeffding radius.  This step treats the entire response vector of one unit as
one bounded variable and asserts no calendar-score independence.

Put \(q=Sd\).  Spectral clipping gives
\(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I_q\).  Each fold has size at least
\(N/3\), so donor unbiasedness and \(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_q\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\left[
 N\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2^2\right]
 \le\frac{6qC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.                                 \tag{4}
\]
This uses the deterministic eigenvalue bound after clipping and does not
require independence of the sample mean and covariance estimate.  Markov's
inequality, a union bound over at most two folds, and the definition of
\(q_{\mathrm{don}}\) imply
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_\ell
 \|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2
 >q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.                                       \tag{5}
\]
On the complement, \(\widehat\Sigma\preceq2C_\Sigma I_q\) and
nonexpansiveness of projection imply
\(\max_\ell\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2\le CN^{-1/2}\).

At a selected local-constant fit, nonnegative unit-mass weights and kernel
support give
\[
 \left|\sum_tw_{st}^{(\ell)}m_s(X_{st})
       -m_s(\widetilde z_{\ell s})\right|
 \le C\{\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
          +\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda\}.                          \tag{6}
\]
Holder continuity from \(\widetilde z_{\ell s}\) to \(z_{0s}\), (5), and
the defining domination of \(C_H\) bound the deterministic error by
\(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Combining (3), (5), and
\(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha\) proves coverage on
the regular branch.  Every declared bad branch returns \([-2B,2B]\), which
contains the target.  Intersecting a covering interval with this known range
preserves coverage.  Thus coverage is uniform over all fixed query values
and kernels, and in particular implies the stated asymptotic display.

For expected length, on the regular branch
\(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\), so, with
\(A=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\),
\[
 r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}
 \le C(\alpha,B)A^{1/2}.                                         \tag{7}
\]
Indeed, the square-root term has this order and
\(\max_s\pi_s/n_s\le A^{1/2}\).  Whenever the reference anchor is
available, certificate optimality gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{bias}}
 \le C\sum_s\pi_s\left\{(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\right\}.                    \tag{8}
\]
Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, projection contraction, and Jensen yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\le CN^{-\lambda/2}.         \tag{9}
\]
Taking expectations in (8) and applying the uniform fixed-query anchor
moment bound gives
\[
 \sup_{z_0}\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}})
 \le C\left[\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 +\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}
 +N^{-\lambda/2}\right].                                        \tag{10}
\]
Along the stated growth arrays the deterministic small-sample branches
vanish.  The remaining fallback event has probability at most \(CT^{-2}\),
and interval length is always at most \(4B\).  Equations (7)--(10) and the
smoothing domination in \texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram} prove
\[
 \sup_{z_0}\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)
 \le CR_\star^{1/2}.                                              \tag{11}
\]
The independent-calendar part of the anchor lemma replaces the logarithmic
term by \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).

For the converse, suppose two laws with targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) have
a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta>2\alpha\).  Uniform
coverage \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under both laws gives
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I_\alpha\}\ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).
\]
Every interval on this event has length at least
\(|\theta_1-\theta_0|\), hence
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)
 \ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.                   \tag{12}
\]
The treated pair used in the marginal proof can be chosen with Hellinger
affinity, and therefore common mass, arbitrarily close to one by reducing
\(\gamma\).  Both kernels have one fixed query, so (12) gives
\(cA^{1/2}\).

For the donor channel, apply
\texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} with
\(\eta\in(2\alpha,1)\), and denote its two mean values by
\(z^{(0)}\) and \(z^{(1)}\).  Under both alternatives use independent
uniform exact designs and the same positive bounded regression
\(m(x)=b_0+a_0|x_k-z^{(0)}_k|^\lambda\) in the displaced cohort, with
constant regressions elsewhere, deterministic responses
\(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\), a common positive treated wealth, and untreated
event wealth \(m_s(z^{(v)}_s)\) under alternative \(v\).
Small \(a_0,b_0\) verify boundedness and the Holder restriction; baseline
wealth one and the horizon-zero construction verify buy-and-hold wealth.
Thus the two fixed-query kernels belong to the union over
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), their panel coordinates coincide, their
donor laws have common mass at least \(\eta\), and their targets differ by
\(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Equation (12) gives the donor lower bound.

Finally, \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies at
one fixed query a common mass above \(2\alpha\) and separation
\(c\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\).  Equation (12), followed by smoothing
domination, yields \(cR_\star^{1/2}\).  In the independent-calendar class,
the no-hit construction in the marginal proof can use a sufficiently small
cube so that its common mass exceeds \(2\alpha\), giving
\(cT^{-\lambda/d}\).  These three pairs establish the uniformly honest
expected-length lower bound.

For a panel law, the fixed-query membership and equality
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau\) hold on the full-marginal-measure query set
proved in \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier}.  Applying the kernel coverage
and length bounds there proves the causal transfer and makes no assertion at
a null query.

Fix a cohort \(s\), an admissible query \(z_0\), and
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  All probabilities below are
under \(\mathbb K_\xi\).  Since \(0<\lambda\le1\), the order convention
gives \(r=0\), so \(G_{sT}(z_{0s},b)\) is scalar.  By continuity and local
positivity of \(K\), there are \(k_0>0\) and
\(\eta\in(0,\delta_0]\) such that \(K(v)\ge k_0\) when
\(\|v\|_2\le\eta\).  Hence \(B(z_{0s},\eta b)\) is inside the cube for
every \(b\le1\).  The Lebesgue-almost-everywhere conditional density lower
bound in the fixed-query class gives, uniformly in \(t\),
\[
 p_{tb}:=\Pr\{\|X_{st}-z_{0s}\|_2\le\eta b\}
 \ge c_Xv_d\eta^db^d=:c_pb^d.                                    \tag{1}
\]
If \(M_b\) counts these visits, then
\[
 G_{sT}(z_{0s},b)\ge\frac{k_0M_b}{Tb^d}.                           \tag{2}
\]

Set
\[
 a_T=\left\lceil\frac{3\log(T\vee2)}{|\log\rho_0|}\right\rceil.
\]
Partition the calendar into consecutive blocks of length \(a_T\) and split
the complete blocks by parity.  In either parity, adjacent retained blocks
are separated by at least \(a_T\) indices.  The definition of beta mixing,
followed by induction over retained blocks, bounds the total variation
distance between their joint law and the product of their marginal block
laws by the sum of the intervening beta coefficients.  Simultaneously for
both parities this distance is at most
\[
 2\left\lceil\frac{T}{a_T}\right\rceil\beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}
 \le CT^{-2}.                                                       \tag{3}
\]
This comparison concerns only design blocks; it neither conditions on nor
decouples response blocks.

For one independent comparison block, let \(Y_j\in[0,a_T]\) be its number
of visits.  The chord bound for the convex function
\(y\mapsto e^{-y/a_T}\) and (1) give
\[
 \mathbb E e^{-Y_j/a_T}
 \le1-\frac{1-e^{-1}}{a_T}\mathbb EY_j
 \le\exp(-cb^d).                                                   \tag{4}
\]
Exponential Markov applied to the independent comparison blocks, separately
by parity, followed by (3), gives constants \(c_1,C_1>0\) such that
\[
 \Pr\{M_b\le c_1Tb^d\}
 \le C_1\exp(-c_1Tb^d/a_T)+C_1T^{-2}                              \tag{5}
\]
when \(Tb^d\ge C_1a_T\); enlarging \(C_1\) makes the bound trivial below
that scale.  Compatibility of \(c_G\) with the population local-constant
Gram lower bound makes (2) at least \(c_G\) off the event in (5).

Put
\[
 b_\circ=(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\vee N^{-1/2}
          \vee(a_T/T)^{1/d}.                                      \tag{6}
\]
The smallest dyadic candidate not below a number in \([b_{0s},1]\) is no
more than twice that number.  Apply (5) at the dyadic scales of order
\(2^jb_\circ\).  The product-block approximation in (3) is made once, so
its \(CT^{-2}\) error is not multiplied by the number of scales.  A union
bound for the independent exponential tails gives
\[
 \Pr\{h_s^\star>C2^jb_\circ\}
 \le C\exp(-c2^{jd})+CT^{-2},\qquad j\ge0,                         \tag{7}
\]
until the scale reaches one; beyond one the probability is zero.  Dyadic
tail summation, with the common coupling-failure event separated before the
sum, yields
\[
 \mathbb E(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}
 \le Cb_\circ^{2\lambda}+CT^{-2}.                                 \tag{8}
\]
When \(b_\circ\) is bounded away from zero, the same conclusion follows
directly from \(h_s^\star\le1\).  Since
\(a_T\le C\log(T\vee2)\) and \(2\lambda/d\le2\), (6)--(8) imply
\[
 \mathbb E(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}
 \le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}+N^{-\lambda}
 +\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)^{2\lambda/d}\right\}.       \tag{9}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives the first-moment assertion.

At \(b=1\), (1)--(5) imply
\(\Pr\{G_{sT}(z_{0s},1)<c_G\}\le CT^{-2}\).  If this fails for no
cohort, \((z_{0s},1)\) is in every fold--cohort anchor set, so fallback is
impossible.  A union bound over fixed \(S\) proves
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}})\le CT^{-2}.         \tag{10}
\]
All constants above are uniform over the fixed-query class because its
density and beta-mixing constants are uniform.  In the independent-calendar
subclass take \(a_T=1\) and omit (3), which replaces the last term in (9) by
\(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  Finally, the definition of the fixed-query class and
the almost-everywhere query conditions put the regular conditional kernel of
each panel law in this class for almost every query, proving the stated
transfer.

Write
\[
 \rho_s=\rho_{sX}(z_{0s}),\qquad
 D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_s^\lambda,
 \qquad A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}.                       \tag{1}
\]
Take a feasible \((f,g,z)\) in \texttt{def:joint-product-modulus} and put
\(q_s=f_s-g_s\).  If \(t_s\) is a nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\),
the nonnegative response budget gives
\[
 |q_s(X_{st_s})|^2\le\sum_{t=1}^{T}|q_s(X_{st})|^2\le n_s^{-1}.    \tag{2}
\]
The difference of two functions in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) is
\(\lambda\)-Holder with constant at most \(2L\).  Thus
\[
 |q_s(z_{0s})|\le n_s^{-1/2}+2L\rho_s^\lambda.                     \tag{3}
\]
The donor budget and \(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\) give
\[
 \|z-z_0\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z-z_0)\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}.                                     \tag{4}
\]
Splitting at \(g_s(z_{0s})\), using (3)--(4), Holder continuity,
\(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), and Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\mathcal T(f,z_0)-\mathcal T(g,z)|
 &\le\sum_s\pi_s|q_s(z_{0s})|
     +L\sum_s\pi_s\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda\\
 &\le C\{A^{1/2}+D_X+N^{-\lambda/2}\}.
\end{aligned}                                                       \tag{5}
\]
Here \(\sum_s\pi_sn_s^{-1/2}\le S^{1/2}A^{1/2}\), and \(S\) is fixed.
Taking the supremum proves the upper modulus bound.  The same argument with
one cohort and no donor displacement proves the asserted upper bound for
\(\omega_{s,X}\).

For the fixed-design lower bound, let
\(\mathcal X_s=\{X_{s1},\ldots,X_{sT}\}\) and define
\[
 q_s(x)=a\,\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal X_s)^\lambda,             \tag{6}
\]
where \(a>0\) is sufficiently small in terms of \(B,L,d\).  Distance to a
closed set is one-Lipschitz, and, for nonnegative \(u,v\),
\[
 |u^\lambda-v^\lambda|\le|u-v|^\lambda                             \tag{7}
\]
because \(0<\lambda\le1\).  Hence \(f_s=q_s/2\) and \(g_s=-q_s/2\)
belong to \(\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}\), agree at every design site, and
differ at \(z_{0s}\) by \(a\rho_s^\lambda\).  Taking \(z=z_0\) uses zero
testing budget and gives
\[
 \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\ge aD_X,\qquad
 \omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})\ge a\rho_s^\lambda.                        \tag{8}
\]

Assume now \(\delta_0<1/2\).  For the donor lower bound choose a coordinate
direction \(v\) pointing into the cube and a fixed positive constant
\[
 a_0\le\frac12\min\{c_\Sigma^{1/2},1/2-\delta_0\},
 \qquad u_N=a_0N^{-1/2}v.
\]
Then \(z_0+u_N\) is admissible and
\[
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2

\(cN^{-\lambda/2}\), including the fixed positive weight of the selected

\[

\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}=A\vee\Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)^2\), prove
\[

Put \(q=Sd\).  Choose a coordinate vector \(e\), with its sign directed
toward \(1/2\) in that coordinate, and set
\[

\]
Choose an orthogonal matrix \(O\) sending the first standard basis vector to
\(w\).  Because \(B^4>q^2\), choose
\(\epsilon\in(0,B^4-q^2)\) and put \(a=(1+\epsilon)^{1/2}>1\).
For real \(u\) near zero, define \(A_u\in\{-a,0,a\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a^2}+\frac{u}{2a},\qquad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a^2}-\frac{u}{2a},\qquad

\]
At \(u=0\) these probabilities are strictly positive, so they remain
probabilities for \(|u|\le u_0\), for some \(u_0>0\).  Direct summation gives
\[

\(V_u=O(A_u,R_2,\ldots,R_q)^\top\).  Then
\[

\]
Orthogonal invariance and independence yield
\[

\]
At \(u=0\), (4) equals
\(a^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2+\epsilon<B^4\).  Its left side is continuous
in \(u\), so, after decreasing \(u_0\), it is at most \(B^4\) throughout
\([-u_0,u_0]\).

Let \(G_u\) be the law of
\[

\]
Equations (3)--(4) give
\[

 \quad\operatorname{Var}(Z_u)=\Sigma,                              \tag{5}

and the required standardized fourth-moment bound.

The Hellinger affinity between \(G_0\) and \(G_u\) is
\[

\]
The three probabilities stay bounded away from zero near zero, so
\(a_H\) has a bounded second derivative there.  Moreover
\(a_H(0)=1\) and
\(a_H'(0)=\tfrac12\sum_rp_r'(0)=0\).  Taylor's theorem gives
\(a_H(u)\ge1-Cu^2\).  Hence, when \(CNu^2\le1/2\),
\[

\]
For dominated laws, Cauchy--Schwarz applied to
\(|p-g|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt g|(\sqrt p+\sqrt g)\) gives
\[
 \|P-G\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\left\{1-\left(\int\sqrt{pg}\right)^2\right\}^{1/2}.        \tag{7}
\]
Choose \(c_\eta>0\) small enough that (6)--(7), with
\(u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}\), give total variation at most \(1-\eta\), and
also choose \(c_\eta\le u_0\).  From (5),
\[

\]
Ellipticity implies
\(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2^{-1}\le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\).  Because the
coordinate moves toward \(1/2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\), (5) remains in the

\(G_0=G_{u=0}\), \(G_1=G_{u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}}\), and enlarging

proposed.name: Fixed-query conditional-kernel class
proposed.construction:
Let
\[
 \mathcal Z_{\delta_0}
 =\left\{z=(z_1^\top,\ldots,z_S^\top)^\top\in([0,1]^d)^S:
 \min_{1\le s\le S}\operatorname{dist}(z_s,\partial[0,1]^d)
 \ge\delta_0\right\}.
\]
For each fixed \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}\), define
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) to be the class of labelled conditional
kernels \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\) for the observed array
\[
 \bigl((B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i},(X_{st})_{s,t},
       (Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\bigr)
\]
at the fixed query \(z_0\).  The label satisfies
\(\mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\),
\(m_s(x)=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[Q_{sti}\mid X_{st}=x]\), and
\(\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_\xi}(Z_j)\).  The kernel, with the
query adjoined as the constant \(z_0\), must satisfy pointwise at this query
all member properties listed in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}.  In
particular: \(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\vee|Q_{sti}|\le B\); every
\(m_s\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\); every \(X_{st}\) has a density
\(f_{st\mid z_0}\) satisfying \(c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X\) for
Lebesgue-almost-every \(x\), uniformly in \(s,t\); the design sequence of
each cohort has \(\beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\).  With
\(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{st})_{s,t})\), conditional on \(\mathcal X\) the
unit histories are independent across \((s,i)\) and obey
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]=\mu_s;
\]
and the donor sample is independent of the complete joint panel, is i.i.d.,
and obeys
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}Z_j=z_0,
 \qquad c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\le B^4.
\]
The historical paths are observed exactly.  Membership also requires an
extension by the potential wealth and return variables obeying consistency,
event-date transport, bounded wealth, and \texttt{def:buyhold-level}; this
makes every causal regular conditional kernel a member while leaving the
statistical functional below distinct from the causal target.  Expectations
and probabilities indexed by \(\xi\) are taken under \(\mathbb K_\xi\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This class makes fixed-query conditional risk and coverage version invariant while retaining exactly the active panel restrictions through deterministic-query extensions.

proposed.construction:

\[
 \theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)
 =\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
