law of the query.
proposed.justification: Conditional density supplies local mass at every named kernel query, and conditional design mixing alone permits a finite block-product comparison for occupancy.
proposed.gap: The no-log spacing conclusion requires conditional independence of design dates at the fixed query.
proposed.consumer: The fixed-query marginal risk and expected-length theorems integrate the anchor certificate through this uniform moment bound.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The dependency graph must name the fixed-query class and its almost-everywhere panel transfer.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\),
\(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\), and fix the class constants.  For every deterministic
exact design \(X=(X_{st})\), every interior reference path \(z_0\), and
every \(c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\), consider
the deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) in
\texttt{def:fixed-design-induced-experiment}.  Its nearest-design estimator
satisfies
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right]
 \le
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right]
 \le C\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
          \vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\right\}.
\]
If \(\delta_0<1/2\), the last display is at most
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)\).  If in addition
\(B^4>(Sd)^2\), then
\[
 cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right].
\]
Neither bound uses a lower local-modulus condition.

For every fixed admissible \(z_0\) and every
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), the conditional law under
\(\mathbb K_\xi\) given the exact design, with its labels, belongs to
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) for \(\mathbb K_\xi\)-almost every design,
and \(\theta_{\mathfrak E}=\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\).  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}
 -\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2\mid(X_{st})\right]
 \le C\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
          \vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\right\}
\]
for almost every design; under \(\delta_0<1/2\), its right side is at most
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).  If every cohort design contains \(z_{0s}\)
exactly, the displayed risk is at most
\(C\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\vee N^{-\lambda}\}\), and
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le C\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\vee N^{-\lambda}\}\).
If instead \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every cohort, then
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2
 \mid(X_{st})\right]\le CR_D,
 \qquad R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D.
\]
No converse in terms of \(R_D\) is asserted.

For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its labelled observed regular
conditional kernel belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for
almost every admissible \(z_0\) under the marginal law of the query, and
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) there by
\texttt{lem:causal-identification}.  Hence all preceding conditional upper
bounds transfer to \(P\) at those query values and at
\(P(\cdot\mid z_0)\)-almost every exact design; no conditional version at a
null query is selected.
proposed.justification: The theorem constructs the bounded replicated-response and full-covariance donor product experiment, gives an explicit nearest-site rule, and bridges first to named fixed-query kernels and then almost everywhere to causal panel laws.
proposed.gap: Donoho's known Gaussian convex experiment and Akhavan et al.'s strongly convex estimated-minimizer problem do not supply this bounded product experiment, external full-covariance query, nearest-site geometry, or almost-everywhere causal bridge.
proposed.consumer: The marginal theorem combines its conditional upper mechanism with uniform fixed-query occupancy and explicit global witnesses.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem now separates deterministic statistical recovery, fixed-query conditional kernels, and the almost-everywhere causal bridge.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\).  For every fixed exact
design \(X=(X_{st})\), every admissible \(z_0\), and every
\(c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\),
\[
 \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)
 \le C\left\{A^{1/2}+D_X(z_0)+N^{-\lambda/2}\right\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})
 \le n_s^{-1/2}+2L\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda,
 \qquad
 \omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})\ge c\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda,
\]
and \(\Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\ge cD_X(z_0)\).  If
\(\delta_0<1/2\), then also
\[
 \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\ge cN^{-\lambda/2},
 \qquad
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 \asymp A\vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
Without strict interior slack, only the always-valid upper characterization
\[
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 \le C\{A\vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\}
\]
is asserted.  Regardless of strict slack, if \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every
\(s\), then \(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)\le CR_D\).
proposed.justification: Distance-function witnesses and nearest-site bounds identify the computable content of the fixed-design product modulus, with the donor-direction equivalence stated on its exact strict-interior regime.
proposed.gap: The distance witness uses rough Holder smoothness, and the donor lower direction requires \(\delta_0<1/2\).
proposed.consumer: The conditional frontier compares its feasible estimator and lower subexperiments to the modulus when strict interior slack is available and to the explicit upper scale otherwise.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The node's claim and free-symbol closure must record the strict-interior premise needed for its donor lower direction.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\), and
\(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\).  Uniformly over fixed admissible query values and their
conditional-kernel classes, the anchor estimator obeys
\[
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \le CR_\star.
\]
The estimator is a single data-measurable rule and does not use the query or
nuisance labels.  This upper bound uses no lower local-modulus condition.  If
\(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\), then, still over the base Holder class,
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2]
 \asymp R_\star
 \asymp
 \left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}
 \vee\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
 \vee N^{-\lambda},
\]
where the infimum is over one data-measurable rule chosen before both
suprema.  Thus the nonredundant oracle/generated-proxy boundary is
\[
 N^{-\lambda}\asymp
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\right\}
 \vee\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}.
\]
The smoothing component in \(R_{\mathrm{or}}\) is algebraically dominated
for fixed \(S\) and is not a fourth nonredundant phase.  On the fixed-query
independent-calendar subclasses, both spacing displays replace the
logarithmic term by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  In the scalar specialization
\(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\), the unreduced bookkeeping form is
\[
 n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}
 \vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda},
\]
and its second term is dominated by the maximum of the first and third.

Separately, for every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its labelled
regular conditional kernel belongs to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost every query under the marginal
law of \(z_0\).  At each such query,
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) and the displayed upper-risk conclusion
applies to \(P(\cdot\mid z_0)\).  No supremum over \(P\)-specific null
conditional values is asserted.
proposed.justification: For rough Holder smoothness, one data-only anchor rule attains the treated-replication, query-conditional spacing, and donor-location maximum uniformly over named fixed-query kernels.
proposed.gap: The conditional mixing envelope incurs a logarithmic spacing term; fixed-query design independence removes it, while higher smoothness is not claimed.
proposed.consumer: Applications can locate the oracle/generated-proxy boundary without selecting null regular-conditional versions or imposing a lower local modulus.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The headline risk and minimax displays must range over the fixed-query kernel experiment, with the causal panel conclusion stated separately almost everywhere.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\),
\(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\).  Along every growth array with
\(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), the total interval \(C_\alpha\)
in \texttt{def:honest-interval} satisfies
\[
 \liminf
 \inf_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \inf_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \Pr_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \{\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\in C_\alpha\}
 \ge1-\alpha,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)]
 \le CR_\star^{1/2}.
\]
These conclusions use no lower local-modulus condition, count the full-range
interval on every declared bad-sample branch, and never divide by an
estimated variance.  If \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\), every single
data-measurable random interval \(I_\alpha\) having the same uniform
fixed-query-kernel coverage obeys
\[
 \sup_{z_0\in\mathcal Z_{\delta_0}}
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)]
 \ge cR_\star^{1/2}
\]
for all sufficiently large indices.  On the fixed-query
independent-calendar subclasses, both upper and lower spacing terms are
\(T^{-\lambda/d}\).  The theorem makes no higher-order claim for
\(\lambda>1\).

For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its labelled regular
conditional kernel is in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost
every query under the marginal law of \(z_0\), and
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) there.  Therefore the coverage and
expected-length upper conclusions apply to \(P(\cdot\mid z_0)\) at those
query values.  No claim is made about a chosen conditional version at a null
query.
proposed.justification: The interval concentrates whole bounded unit histories, then adds Holder and full-covariance donor radii uniformly over the fixed-query kernel experiment.
proposed.gap: Armstrong--Kolesar ordered-modulus and bias-aware intervals concern ordinary regression, while Cattaneo--Feng--Titiunik study dependent synthetic-control prediction; neither gives this generated-query unit-history interval or donor expected-length converse.
proposed.consumer: The procedure is conditionally honest without calendar-score decoupling and transfers to causal laws only at their almost-everywhere regular query kernels.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Coverage and expected length now have a version-invariant fixed-query domain and an explicit almost-everywhere causal transfer.

proposed_core_edits.proposed:
The causal target remains
\(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\mathbb E[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\).
Consistency and event-date transport imply, rather than define, its equality
with the observed-law functional \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\).
For each fixed admissible query, random-design risk, coverage, and expected
length are stated uniformly over the labelled conditional-kernel class
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), and the minimax decision rule is one
data-measurable rule chosen before taking the supremum over query values.
The deterministic fixed-design experiment has minimax mean squared error
\(\asymp R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\) under the stated converse slack and admits the
nearest-design upper witness for every fixed design.  For
\(0<\lambda\le1\), the anchor estimator has marginal squared risk at most
\(CR_\star\), and the unit-history interval is uniformly conditionally
honest with expected length at most \(CR_\star^{1/2}\); the matching
fixed-query-kernel converses hold under the stated strict interior and donor
moment slack.  Separately, for every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its
labelled regular conditional kernel belongs to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost every query under the marginal
law of \(z_0\), and the kernel conclusions transfer there with
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau\).  No supremum over law-specific null
conditional versions is taken.  No headline result assumes a lower local
modulus, and no claim is made for \(\lambda>1\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The metadata must distinguish the observed-law fixed-query functional from the causal estimand and must not advertise suprema over law-specific null conditional versions.
